# Model Card — Ethicura AI Deepfake Detector (v2)

*Following the Model Card framework by Mitchell et al. (2019). Every number below comes from [`results/`](../results), generated by [`training/run.py`](../training/run.py).*

---

## Model Details

| Field | Details |
|-------|---------|
| Model name | Ethicura AI — EfficientNetB0 Deepfake Classifier |
| Version | 2.0 (October 2026) |
| File | [`models/ethicura_effnetb0.keras`](../models/ethicura_effnetb0.keras); ONNX export for the browser in [ethicura-frontend](https://github.com/a77chand/ethicura-frontend) |
| Architecture | MTCNN face crop (20% margin) → EfficientNetB0 (ImageNet init) → global average pool → dropout 0.3 → dense(sigmoid). Grad-CAM over the EfficientNet feature map for explanations |
| Input | One face crop, 224×224 RGB, scaled to [0, 1] |
| Output | P(fake), Platt-calibrated (scale and shift folded into the final layer) |
| Developed by | Anusha Chandra & Revanth Christober M |
| Organisation | The Junior Academy, New York Academy of Sciences |
| Previous version | v1: XceptionNet on FaceForensics++ (see [History](#history-v1)) |

---

## Intended Use

**Primary use:** A *warning signal* that a face in an image or video frame may have been generated or manipulated. It's meant for people checking social media, educational content and professional contexts, with a human making the final call.

**Out-of-scope uses:**
- **Legal evidence** or definitive proof of manipulation. This is a warning tool, not a court-grade forensic system.
- **Real-time mass surveillance.**
- **Deployment against marginalised communities** without their consent.
- **Manipulation types far from the training data.** Performance drops sharply out of domain (see below).

---

## Training Data

- **[DeepFakeFace](https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenRL/DeepFakeFace)** (OpenRAIL): 30k real IMDB-WIKI celebrity photos, each with one fake from each of three generators:
  - Stable Diffusion inpainting
  - InsightFace face swap
  - Stable Diffusion text-to-image
- **Splits:** by person, 80/10/10, so no identity appears in two splits.
- **Shortcut controls:**
  - Grayscale images are dropped from every class, because grayscale was unevenly distributed between real and fake.
  - Every image goes through the API's own MTCNN crop and is re-encoded identically.
  - Faces under 80 px wide are dropped.
- **Augmentation, applied to both classes:** flip, face-box jitter, brightness, contrast and saturation changes, random downscaling, and JPEG recompression at quality 35–100.
- **Training set size:** 15,296 real faces per epoch, matched by an equal number of fakes split evenly across the three generators.
- **Schedule:** 1 epoch training the head on the frozen backbone, then 8 epochs fine-tuning everything (AdamW, cosine decay), on a Kaggle GPU. The best epoch is chosen by validation AUC.

---

## Evaluation

**Test set:** 1,838 real and 6,219 fake faces from **people never seen in training**. The 95% confidence intervals come from a person-level bootstrap.

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| AUC | **0.986** (0.984–0.988) |
| Equal error rate | 5.6% |
| Fakes caught at 1% / 5% false alarms | 82.7% / 94.0% |
| Balanced accuracy at 0.5 | 94.6% |
| Calibration error (ECE, class-balanced) | 0.011 |

**Per generator (AUC):**
- SD inpainting: 0.986
- InsightFace swap: 0.987
- SD text-to-image: 0.986

**Robustness:** AUC is 0.968 or above under JPEG quality 30, and 0.91 or above under ×0.25 downscaling or Gaussian blur with σ = 2.

**Generalisation:**
- **Unseen generators:** a model trained without a generator scores as follows on it:
  - SD inpainting: 0.939
  - SD text-to-image: 0.946
  - InsightFace swap: **0.765**
- **Cross-dataset:** on [SDFVD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Hemgg/SDFVD-video-dataset) (53 real and 53 commercial face-swap videos), video-level AUC is **0.63** (0.56–0.70).

**Baseline:** the third-party model this replaces scores AUC 0.48 on the same test set, which is chance level.

---

## Limitations

1. **Out-of-domain manipulations.** It performs well on the three generators it was trained on, but weakly on unseen face-swap pipelines (0.765) and on a different video dataset (0.63). Expect similar or worse results on newer generators, other face-swap tools and lip-sync fakes.
2. **Frame-by-frame only.** There's no temporal model, so it can't detect inconsistencies across frames. Video verdicts are averages of per-frame scores.
3. **Celebrity photos.** The real images are IMDB-WIKI press and event photos, unlike webcam footage (lighting, sensors, compression). The live webcam demo is therefore out of domain in a mild way.
4. **Face detector sensitivity.** Scores depend on the crop. Measured on the full test set, the browser pipeline (BlazeFace) reaches AUC 0.982 against 0.986 with MTCNN, and misses the face in 2.2% of images. Individual frames of turned heads can still flip near the 50% line.
5. **Faces under about 80 px** were excluded from training and testing, so very small or distant faces are unvalidated.
6. **Adversarial attacks.** The model isn't hardened against perturbations designed to fool it.

---

## Bias & Fairness Considerations

- **No subgroup evaluation.** IMDB-WIKI has no reliable demographic labels, so per-group performance hasn't been measured. Don't assume equal error rates across skin tones, ages or genders.
- **Possible skew.** IMDB-WIKI over-represents Western celebrities. Evaluate on your own population before relying on it.
- **Shortcut checks.** Grad-CAM heatmaps help check whether the model attends to the face rather than background or other spurious cues. The shortcut controls above remove the confounds that the dataset inspection found.

---

## Ethical Use Statement

Ethicura AI is built with transparency and human agency at its core. The Grad-CAM layer makes the model's reasoning visible, and the in-browser demo processes video on-device without uploading it. The system is designed to **warn, not decide**. Any deployment must:

- Inform users that content is being analysed
- Present calibrated confidence scores rather than hard verdicts
- Provide a path for appeal or human review
- Not be used to target or harass individuals

---

## History: v1

The project began with an XceptionNet fine-tuned on FaceForensics++ (299×299 input). It reported accuracy 95%, precision 93%, recall 92%, F1 92.5% and AUC 0.97, benchmarked against MesoNet, CapsuleNet, FWA and others. Those weights were never committed to the repository, so v1 can't be re-evaluated or compared directly with v2.
